checked_claims.claim: AST restrictions guarantee safe Python library execution
checked_claims.reason: Intentional trusted-code extension executes modules; allowlists/AST filtering alone cannot sandbox arbitrary Python.

material_errors: Intentional trusted-code extension executes modules; allowlists/AST filtering alone cannot sandbox arbitrary Python.
tasks.notes: Static inspection of pinned source; no upstream code execution.
tasks.corrected_reference_answer: The loader executes discovered modules with exec_module (src/sqlfluff/core/templaters/jinja.py:274-289), so library_path is a trusted-code extension boundary, not protected by Jinja's template sandbox. The repository recommends invocation-level configuration overrides or --library-path none for secure deployments (docs/source/production/security.rst:31-48). A redesign should disable untrusted library loading by default and permit administrator-controlled trusted libraries explicitly. If arbitrary untrusted Python must run, use an external process/container boundary with OS-enforced filesystem, network and resource restrictions; path/name allowlists, export checks and AST scans are defense-in-depth rather than sufficient execution isolation.
